conventions.convention: Assume inherited AC and a characteristic-zero coefficient field. The quiver is finite and loopless; parallel arrows and arrows in both directions are allowed. The dimension vector belongs to N^I, including zero.
Flags increase, with quotient at position r having color ν_r. Stable arrow entries run from position a to position b with a>b. Thus d_ν is the flag dimension plus the sum of h_{ν_aν_b} over a>b.
The first coordinate is the categorical source: e_η A e_ν=Ext_G(L_η,L_ν). Multiplication is a*b=b[n]∘a for homogeneous a of degree n. Ext degree n corresponds to BM degree d_η+d_ν−n.

Dots are first Chern classes of the quotient lines themselves. Fundamental classes retain positive complex orientation. Equal-color τ is minus the standard elementary fundamental class; distinct-color τ is the standard class after the two specified sign normalizations cancel.

Q_ii=0 and Q_ij(u,v)=(-1)^{h_ij}(u−v)^{h_ij+h_ji} for i≠j. Equal-color mixed relations have signs +1 and −1. The outer-equal braid difference is τ_{r+1}τ_rτ_{r+1}−τ_rτ_{r+1}τ_r, with correction [Q(x_r,x_{r+1})−Q(x_{r+2},x_{r+1})]/(x_{r+2}−x_r).

P_ν=H_G^•(X_ν;k)[d_ν], so its unit has degree −d_ν. Dots have degree 2 and crossings degree −a_{ν_rν_{r+1}}. PBW products use one fixed reduced expression for each permutation; independence of the resulting product from that choice is not asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Assume inherited AC and the setting of the defining item. The convolution algebra acts faithfully on P=⊕_ν H_G^•(X_ν;k)[d_ν], with H_G^•(X_ν;k)=k[x_1,…,x_m]. For one fixed reduced expression of every w∈S_m, the elements x_1^{c_1}⋯x_m^{c_m}τ_w e_ν, c_r≥0, form a k-basis; equivalently, the crossing products form a free basis over the first-coordinate polynomial corners acting by left multiplication. Dots and elementary crossings generate the algebra. Only relative-position incidence strata are paved.

For a finite loopless quiver, β∈N^I and a characteristic-zero field, under inherited AC, defines stable graded full-flag incidence spaces X_ν, d_ν, L_ν=π_{ν!}k[d_ν], source-first corners and opposite-composition multiplication, diagonal and quotient-line Chern classes, normalized elementary correspondence classes, and the intrinsic signed presentation S_Γ(β) with Q_ij(u,v)=(-1)^{h_ij}(u−v)^{h_ij+h_ji}.

Assume inherited AC and the defining item's setting. The geometric generators satisfy every relation of S_Γ(β). On shifted polynomial summands, equal-color crossings act by (f−s_rf)/(x_r−x_{r+1}), and distinct-color crossings on the ν-summand act by (x_r−x_{r+1})^{h_ij}s_r(f), with values in the s_rν-summand. Their degrees are 0, 2 and −a_{ν_rν_{r+1}}, yielding a graded homomorphism S_Γ(β)→A.

Assume inherited AC and let Γ, β and k be as in the defining item. There is a unique graded k-algebra isomorphism S_Γ(β)→Ext_G^•(⊕_ν π_{ν!}k[d_ν],⊕_ν π_{ν!}k[d_ν]) sending the generators to their specified geometric classes, with multiplication a*b=b[n]∘a. Ext degree n in the (η,ν) component corresponds to BM degree d_η+d_ν−n. No semisimplicity, purity or decomposition theorem is used, and total Ext finite-dimensionality is not assumed.

seams_checked.note: Checked both page interfaces and the cited supplier statements and proofs. The incidence spaces meet the properness and smooth pure-dimensional source hypotheses; the source-first corners, opposite shifted composition, normalized dualizing object and BM degree dictionary agree. The batch does not add smoothness or transversality of fiber products, semismallness, purity or decomposition hypotheses.

Checked both pages and the actual geometric consumer, thm-self-dual-indecomposable-klr-projectives-give-the-negative-half-lower-global-basis, especially F3 and Proof 1.1–2.2. It preserves characteristic zero, symmetric quiver normalization, arbitrary arrow multiplicities, native crossing signs, unit degree −d_ν and source-first opposite composition. Semisimplicity is obtained from a separate supplier. The localization, grading and triangular-generation arguments were also compared with [Varagnolo–Vasserot, §§2.20–2.27 and 3.6–3.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0901.3992), retaining this batch's explicit positive-tangent orientation normalization.
